title: Toward Real-life Dialogue State Tracking Involving Negative Feedback Utterances

problem.claim: Dialogue state tracking must parse task-oriented dialogues into slot-value-pair states, including conversations containing user negative feedback that can provide corrective information after system errors.

gap.claim: Existing dialogue state tracking research largely ignores real-life user negative feedback utterances, and datasets involving such utterances are lacking.

contributions.claim: Defines a schema for user negative feedback utterances.
Proposes a joint modeling method for negative feedback utterance generation and filtering.
Explores interaction mechanisms for conversations involving negative feedback utterances and proposes related evaluation metrics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Using simulated negative feedback utterances constructed in training and testing on WOZ2.0 and MultiWOZ2.1, the authors report that negative feedback utterances play an important role in dialogue state tracking.
The authors report an analysis of the advantages and disadvantages of different interaction mechanisms involving negative feedback utterances.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dialogue state tracking is a core component of task-oriented dialogue systems.
Current benchmark-oriented research largely overlooks negative feedback utterances that occur after system errors and may contain corrective information.
The paper studies negative feedback in dialogue state tracking through simulated utterances, introducing a schema and joint generation-filtering model.
It examines interaction mechanisms and evaluation metrics for conversations involving negative feedback.
Experiments with simulated feedback on WOZ2.0 and MultiWOZ2.1 report benefits of negative feedback and compare interaction mechanisms.

source_observation.claim: Negative feedback utterances can contain corrective information after system errors.

interpretation.claim: Error-repair signals from users may be useful inputs for improving dialogue state tracking.

application.claim: Dialogue systems could model, filter, and evaluate user negative feedback as part of state-tracking interactions.

exception.claim: The abstract describes simulated negative feedback and does not establish performance in naturally occurring real-life conversations.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset sizes, model architecture details, evaluation metric definitions, or numerical results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported findings.
